key_insight: World from Motion turns a monocular video into a freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian scene. It uses motion-aware, pixel-aligned conditioning to fix artifacts and recover missing content in dynamic reconstructions.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing dynamic 3D scenes from only a single video, where conventional methods often produce incomplete geometry, rendering artifacts, and poor novel-view synthesis for moving objects and regions outside the original view.
method: Build an initial dynamic 3D Gaussian reconstruction from monocular video.
Condition a video model on dense, pixel-aligned renderings that encode appearance, geometry, and 3D scene motion from both input and target camera paths.
Use the conditioned model to refine renderings, correct artifacts, and hallucinate missing regions for more complete dynamic 3D Gaussian representations.
impact: This enables higher-quality dynamic scene reconstruction and freer novel-view rendering from just a monocular video, which is useful for AR/VR, robotics, digital twins, and content creation. For practitioners, it offers a practical path to more realistic and complete 3D scene generation without requiring multi-camera capture.

paper_title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video
paper_authors: Liyuan Zhu, Shengyu Huang, Amrita Mazumdar, Tianye Li, Zan Gojcic
